clue.text: Pike intervenes misguidedly — stupid boy, 16, as 23 would say

indicators.note: acting misguidedly, the letters of the two words are sent the wrong way and rearranged

explanation.surface: Private Pike from Dad's Army butts in clumsily, earning Mainwaring's catchphrase and a jibe about his loud mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid boy' is Captain Mainwaring's put-down of Pike in the sitcom Dad's Army, which tempts a reading about the show; the anagram of PIKE INTERVENES gives the England batsman who fell out with his captain at 23.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricketer was famously at odds with captain Andrew Strauss, who might call him a foolish loudmouth.

clue.text: Repulsive former English LibDem leader crushing resistance

parts.note: ex- is a prefix meaning former

indicators.note: Cable crushing something squeezes it into the middle of his name

parts.note: Vince Cable led the Liberal Democrats from 2017 to 2019
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A disgusting ex-leader of the Liberal Democrats stamps out all opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something execrable is utterly detestable, so repulsive is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Huge blokes, drunk, semi-clad

indicators.note: clad means the rearranged letters are wrapped like clothing around the blokes
drunk means the letters of semi are reeling about into a new order

parts.note: blokes are men

explanation.surface: Massive men, worse for drink, half dressed after a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-clad' reads as half-dressed, but the hyphen hides two jobs: 'semi' is the fodder and 'clad' wraps it round the blokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means enormous in size or extent, a close synonym of huge.

clue.text: 6 boy safe on sleepover

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
split as sleep over: a nap, a short sleep, turned over to read the other way

explanation.surface: A boy kept safe at a friend's house overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is the answer at 6-down, so '6 boy' is the boy who never grows up; 'sleepover' must be split into 'sleep' and 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie's character never ages, so he is the everlasting boy that 6-down describes.

clue.text: Substitute loading containers at Zeebrugge

indicators.note: the run of words is loading, carrying the answer as cargo inside them

explanation.surface: A replacement is found to load the shipping containers at the Belgian port of Zeebrugge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior replacement or imitation, so it is a substitute.

clue.text: Nice summer rental, saving energy and time without end

parts.note: été is French for summer, as it would be called in Nice

indicators.note: saving in the sense of except: the rental with energy and time left out

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
T is the symbol for time

explanation.surface: A summer let on the Riviera that saves on power bills and goes on for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like keeping but means 'except', removing E and T from RENTAL to leave RNAL; Nice is the French city, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal never finishes, so it lasts without end.

clue.text: Reportedly influenced band

indicators.note: reportedly signals the word for influenced is heard, not seen

parts.note: to be swayed is to be influenced

explanation.surface: A band said to have shaped later music.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede were a leading Britpop group of the 1990s, contemporaries of the theme band.

clue.text: Conk broken by my duck

indicators.note: broken by means the nose is split open with another word inside

parts.note: conk is British slang for a nose
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: Someone's nose is smashed by a duck, to their exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a batsman out without scoring; 'my' is the exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket duck is an innings in which the batsman makes nothing at all.

clue.text: Delia's family group

definitions.meaning: Delia Smith, the British TV cook, and her relatives share her surname
a band: Morrissey and Johnny Marr's 1980s Manchester group

explanation.surface: Delia's family band.
explanation.definitionFit: The cook's household would collectively share her surname, which is also the name of the indie band.

clue.text: Understood 1ac anagram in Times

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters are placed inside the pair of times

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so 'Times' gives two Ts

indicators.note: the word anagram itself tells us the letters before it are shuffled

parts.note: read literally, the figure 1 is the Roman numeral I, followed by the letters AC

explanation.surface: A Times solver understands a reference to the first across answer.
explanation.walkthrough: '1ac' looks like a cross-reference to 1-across but is read literally as I and AC; 'anagram' makes ACI, which goes 'in' T and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is unspoken but implied, i.e. understood without being said.

clue.text: The odds of 7 spades to finish?

indicators.note: to finish sends the spades letter to the end of the word

parts.note: the figure 7 is spelt out as the number word
S is the bridge abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A gambler asks what price they get on seven of spades finishing the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' looks like a cross-reference to 7-down but is just the number; moving its S to the end gives the bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Even money, called evens, is the betting price at which the stake is doubled if it wins.

clue.text: Conservative old individual received by king and queen; he's often in court

indicators.note: received by means the king and queen take the individual in between them

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
R stands for regina, Latin for queen
an individual is one

explanation.surface: An elderly Tory is welcomed by royalty and is regularly seen at court.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a royal court; the court is a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: This official holds inquests into sudden deaths, sitting in a court to do so.

clue.text: Fruit flavour — peeled cantaloupe?

parts.note: a tang is a sharp flavour

indicators.note: peeled means the skin, the outer letters, comes off

parts.note: a cantaloupe is an example of a melon, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: The taste of a cantaloupe once its skin is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' strips the first and last letters from MELON to leave ELO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit, a cross between a tangerine and a pomelo.

clue.text: Thanks! Fresh Melba toast out of the oven — put it on here!

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: fresh means the letters of Melba are made anew in another order
out of means the oven is taken away from the word toast

parts.note: an oast is a kiln or oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: Thanking someone for hot Melba toast and telling them where to set it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' gives BLEMA from MELBA; 'out of' removes OAST from TOAST, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat on the dining table is where you put a hot plate, so it is where to put something down.

clue.text: Pacino first to salute unbeatable service here in France

parts.note: Al Pacino is the American actor

indicators.note: first to salute is its opening letter

parts.note: an ace is a tennis serve the receiver cannot return

explanation.surface: Al Pacino greets a tennis ace in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is a region of north-eastern France, on the German border.

clue.text: Autumn ode composed — it's outstanding

indicators.note: composed means the letters of these two words are put together afresh

explanation.surface: An autumn poem has been written and is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum still owed on a bill is said to be outstanding, still to be paid.

clue.text: Gossip downs tools once more, hit by 9ac

parts.note: a gossip is someone who cannot keep their mouth shut, a blabber
to down tools is to stop work, to strike
once more means a second time

explanation.surface: A gossiping worker walks out once more, struck by the group from 9.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a blow but means a hit single by the band at 9-across.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1986 single is one of the Manchester band's best-known hits.

clue.text: He must've sent Jane bananas!

parts.note: Tarzan, raised by apes, drove Jane wild; 'bananas' is both crazy and the ape's fruit

explanation.surface: A man who must have driven Jane crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan is the jungle hero raised by apes, partner of Jane.

clue.text: As bottom cut short?

parts.note: arse is British slang for bottom

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its final letter

parts.note: a nick is a small cut

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a backside is trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is not a link word but the chemical symbol of the poison.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol of the poisonous element number 33.

clue.text: From Kenya, run delicatessen somewhere in Sussex

indicators.note: from signals the answer is taken out of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A Kenyan runs a deli in an English county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Arundel is a castle town in West Sussex, on the River Arun.

clue.text: Spoken about men in annual mass migration

indicators.note: about means the word for spoken turns round

parts.note: said means spoken

indicators.note: in means the soldiers go inside the yearly abbreviation

parts.note: pa, per annum, means yearly
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A conversation about an annual mass gathering of people on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses SAID to DIAS; 'mass' belongs to the definition, not a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is the dispersal of a people from their homeland, a mass migration.

clue.text: See 16
See 16
K-Pop star's revolutionary spirit

parts.note: Psy is the South Korean singer of Gangnam Style
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A Korean pop star has a rebellious spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind, one's spirit.

clue.text: Composer who got crotchety with 1?

definitions.meaning: Johann or Richard, Austrian and German composers
Andrew, the England cricket captain who fell out with the batsman at 1; 'crotchety' nods to musical crotchets

explanation.surface: A composer who grew irritable with a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to several composers and to the former England captain who clashed with his star batsman.

clue.text: Measure, say, Reading University business degree

parts.note: R is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: Someone measures a business degree from the University of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' is not the English town but the R in the three Rs; a 'measure' is an old word for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is an old term for a dance, of which this Cuban ballroom step is an example.

clue.text: A tempestuous character, mother pocketed R1

indicators.note: pocketed means mother takes the money inside her

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
R is the symbol for the South African rand, so R1 is one rand

explanation.surface: A stormy figure whose mother pockets a single coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tempestuous' means belonging to The Tempest, and 'R1' is a price, one rand, not BBC Radio 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero's daughter is the heroine of Shakespeare's play The Tempest.

clue.text: Order Ms Dorries out — she doesn't belong in The House

definitions.text: she doesn't belong in The House

indicators.note: Ms Dorries is spread out, opened up so the order can sit inside her name

parts.note: Nad is short for Nadine Dorries, the former Conservative MP
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A demand to expel Nadine Dorries, who has no place in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: Nadine Dorries, the former Conservative MP, was nicknamed Mad Nad; The House looks like Parliament, but the definition means a wanderer with no fixed home.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no settled abode has no house to belong in.

clue.text: After 28 maybe dine out, included at no extra cost

indicators.note: after means the rearranged dining word comes after the name

parts.note: the first name at 28 is a form of Charles, and Chuck is another pet form of Charles

indicators.note: out means the letters of dine are put out of order

explanation.surface: Once the comedian has been seen, go out for dinner, everything free.
explanation.walkthrough: '28' is a cross-reference to the comedian's first name, which here stands as a stand-in for another nickname for Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown in with a purchase is given free as an extra.

clue.text: Stupid boy boobs in front of The Queen — he made us laugh

indicators.note: in front of places the earlier pieces before the royal one

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool
the chest is where breasts are found
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A daft lad flashes the Queen, to general laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boobs' looks like blunders but here means breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The British radio and TV comedian was famous from the 1940s to the 1960s for making audiences laugh.
